close_reason: HttpCrlFetcher<F, V> impls pkix_revocation::RevocationChecker. check_revocation extracts HTTP/HTTPS CDP URLs, fetches each via the user-supplied RevocationFetcher, delegates parsed CRL bytes to pkix_revocation::CrlChecker. First successful parse path is determinative; fetch + parse failures fall through; all-failed surfaces as Error::RevocationFetchFailed. Added that new variant to pkix_revocation::Error (std-gated, additive on non_exhaustive enum, pkix-revocation 0.3.1 -> 0.3.2). check_revocation_against_anchor stays at trait default Ok(()) matching CrlChecker. Tests use pyca/cryptography fixtures + closure-mock fetcher: 7 scenarios green. Committed at 4ef429be.
description:
## Why

Wire CDP URL extraction (PKIX-a1yc.2) + RevocationFetcher (PKIX-a1yc.1) + pkix-revocation::CrlChecker into a single RevocationChecker that fetches CRLs from each cert's CDP and delegates revocation checks.

## What

Replace the placeholder `HttpCrlFetcher<F>` with a working impl:

```rust
#[cfg(feature = "crl")]
pub struct HttpCrlFetcher<F, V> {
    fetcher: F,
    verifier: V,
    now_unix: u64,
    // Optional: max CRL size, etc. — deferred to caching child PKIX-a1yc.7
}

#[cfg(feature = "crl")]
impl<F: RevocationFetcher, V: SignatureVerifier + Clone> HttpCrlFetcher<F, V> {
    pub const fn new(fetcher: F, verifier: V, now_unix: u64) -> Self;
}

#[cfg(feature = "crl")]
impl<F: RevocationFetcher, V: SignatureVerifier + Clone> RevocationChecker
    for HttpCrlFetcher<F, V>
{
    fn check_revocation(&self, cert: &Certificate, issuer: &Certificate)
        -> pkix_revocation::Result<()>;

    fn check_revocation_against_anchor(
        &self,
        cert: &Certificate,
        anchor: &TrustAnchor,
    ) -> pkix_revocation::Result<()>;
}
```

### check_revocation flow

1. Extract CDP URLs from cert (via PKIX-a1yc.2 helper). If empty, return Ok(()) — no CDPs means no CRL-based revocation status (document this; a stricter policy can be a follow-up).
2. For each URL in order:
   a. `fetcher.fetch(GET, url)` → bytes (or move on to next URL on FetchError; collect last error to return if all fail).
   b. `CrlChecker::new(bytes, now_unix, verifier.clone())` — if parse error, treat as fetch failure for this URL and continue.
   c. `checker.check_revocation(cert, issuer)` — return result immediately. If revocation status determined (Ok or Err::Revoked), surface that; do not try other URLs.
3. If all URLs failed without yielding a checker, return a new error variant `Error::FetchError(url, source)` or similar (needs to be surfaced through pkix-revocation::Error — coordinate with PKIX-a1yc.1).

### check_revocation_against_anchor flow

Identical, but issuer is `&anchor.cert` (the TrustAnchor's cert reference). The anchor cert is the issuer for an EE that the trust anchor signed directly.

## Acceptance

- [ ] HttpCrlFetcher impls RevocationChecker (and check_revocation_against_anchor).
- [ ] Empty CDP list returns Ok(()) (documented).
- [ ] First successful fetch+parse path is taken; subsequent URLs not fetched.
- [ ] All URLs failing surfaces a clear error variant.
- [ ] Tests with mock RevocationFetcher (canned bytes) covering: revoked cert, good cert, fetcher all-fail, parse error on first URL falls back to second.
- [ ] No new pkix-revocation deps; only x509-cert + der + the parent revocation crate.

## Out of scope

- Caching (PKIX-a1yc.7).
- IDP scope matching — that's already in pkix-revocation::CrlChecker; we just feed it bytes.
- Nondeterministic URL ordering (we walk in extension-defined order).

## Effort

~180 lines + tests.

## Depends on

PKIX-a1yc.1 (trait widening), PKIX-a1yc.2 (CDP extractor).
